item.title: NEW: N0N Extortion Group Claims Breach of 830M Expedia Loyalty Records
item.description:
Headline: N0N Extortion Group Claims Breach of 830M Expedia Loyalty Records

Summary:
The data extortion group N0N has listed Expedia Group on its dark web leak site, claiming to have exfiltrated 830 million records from the company's loyalty program. The group alleges the data includes customer emails, loyalty IDs, and booking values. However, as of November 9, 2026, N0N has not provided any proof to substantiate its claims. Expedia Group has not issued a public statement or filed a material incident report regarding the alleged data exposure. Security analysts advise caution, as such claims are sometimes exaggerated or fabricated.

Severity: High

Categories: Data Breach, Threat Actor, Ransomware

Meta Description: The N0N data extortion group has claimed a major data breach of Expedia Group's loyalty program, allegedly exposing 830 million records. The claim is unverified.

item.title: NEW: Bitter APT Targets South Asia with New C++/Rust PapRAT Backdoor
item.description:
Headline: Bitter APT Targets South Asia with New C++/Rust PapRAT Backdoor

Summary:
The cyber espionage group Bitter (APT-C-08) is conducting a new campaign targeting organizations in South Asia with a previously undocumented remote access trojan (RAT) named PapRAT. The malware, which exists in both C++ and Rust versions, is delivered through complex infection chains involving malicious LNK files, VHDX disk images, and WebDAV servers. PapRAT's capabilities include command execution, file manipulation, and screen capture, demonstrating the threat actor's evolving sophistication and use of living-off-the-land techniques.

Severity: High

Categories: Threat Actor, Malware, Cyberattack

Meta Description: Cyber espionage group Bitter (APT-C-08) is using a new remote access trojan, PapRAT, in a campaign targeting organizations across South Asia with advanced TTPs.

item.title: NEW: Microsoft Revises Windows 11 Paint RCE Flaw, Lowers CVSS Score
item.description:
Headline: Microsoft Revises Windows 11 Paint RCE Flaw, Lowers CVSS Score

Summary:
Microsoft has revised the details for CVE-2026-83844, a remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows 11 Paint app. The CVSS score was lowered from 8.1 to 7.0 after clarifying the attack vector is 'Local', requiring a user to open a malicious file, not 'Network'. The vulnerability, an out-of-bounds read, has no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation. The definitive patch is confirmed to be in Paint version 11.2609.401.0, available via the Microsoft Store.

Severity: Medium

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management

Meta Description: Microsoft has lowered the severity of CVE-2026-83844, a Windows 11 Paint RCE bug, to CVSS 7.0, clarifying that it requires local user interaction to exploit.

item.title: NEW: Critical GitLab RCE Flaw (CVE-2026-97229) Actively Exploited
item.description:
Headline: Critical GitLab RCE Flaw (CVE-2026-97229) Actively Exploited

Summary:
A critical, unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in GitLab (CVE-2026-97229) is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw allows attackers to run arbitrary code by submitting a crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration file. Due to evidence of active exploitation, CISA has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch. Administrators of affected GitLab CE/EE versions are urged to update immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Patch Management

Meta Description: A critical, unauthenticated RCE vulnerability in GitLab (CVE-2026-97229) is under active exploitation and has been added to the CISA KEV catalog. Patch now.

item.title: NEW: SonicWall Patches Actively Exploited VPN Auth Bypass Flaw
item.description:
Headline: SonicWall Patches Actively Exploited VPN Auth Bypass Flaw

Summary:
SonicWall has released urgent security updates for CVE-2026-19868, a high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability in its SonicOS SSL VPN component. The flaw, now on CISA's KEV list, is being actively exploited in the wild. It allows an attacker with valid credentials for an alternate login method to bypass SAML authentication and its associated multi-factor authentication (MFA), significantly weakening security for affected firewall devices. Federal agencies are mandated to patch by November 20, 2026.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Cyberattack

Meta Description: SonicWall releases urgent patches for an actively exploited authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-19868, in SonicOS that allows MFA bypass on SSL VPNs.

Attackers exploited vulnerabilities in Danfoss controllers to manipulate temperature settings, causing product spoilage and highlighting significant risks in operational technology (OT) security. The attacks were preceded by a two-week reconnaissance period, indicating a planned operation against exposed and poorly secured critical infrastructure components.

item.title: UPDATE: CISA Adds Actively Exploited SonicWall MFA Bypass Flaw to KEV Catalog
item.description:
Headline: CISA Adds Actively Exploited SonicWall MFA Bypass Flaw to KEV Catalog

Summary:
The U.S. CISA has added a critical SonicWall SSL-VPN vulnerability, CVE-2026-19868, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, confirming active attacks. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 7.5, allows an attacker with valid credentials for a secondary authentication method to bypass SAML and multi-factor authentication (MFA). Federal agencies are mandated to patch by November 20, 2026, and all organizations using affected SonicWall devices are urged to update immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Security Operations

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: CISA has added SonicWall SSL-VPN vulnerability CVE-2026-19868 to its KEV catalog, confirming active exploitation of the MFA bypass flaw. Patching is urgent.
